value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column action_date
variable_description: The day Centrelink processed the concession card decision that this row records. DSS defines the column as "The date on which a concession card is actioned, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD", which makes it a processing date rather than an entitlement date: CARD_ISSUE_DATE is when the card was produced and CARD_START_DATE is when it could first be used. All four concession card tables carry it, so a card's administrative sequence of action, issue, start and expiry reads the same way for a health care card, a pensioner card, a low income card and a seniors health card.
value_definition: A calendar date written YYYY-MM-DD. The domain is open: any date on which Centrelink actioned a card record, which in DOMINO runs from 2000 to the extract date.
limitation: It does not say what the action was. A grant, a reissue after loss, a variation and a cancellation all stamp this one field, so REASON_CODE and END_REASON_CODE are needed to tell them apart. An action date can also fall either side of the card's own start date, so it cannot stand in for the date entitlement began.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the PLIDA distribution of the health care card table and gives a verbatim definition for the action_date column, alongside the sibling date columns that distinguish it.
evidence_quote: The date on which a concession card is actioned, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Concession card action date', with the generic sentence 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' printed as both the value definition and the limitation, so it never said which of the four card dates this one is.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distributions SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA, item 110613) and STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA, item 84485)
variable_description: A recipient's age in completed years, fixed at a reference date rather than measured at the event on the row. Which reference date depends on the table: STATIC_DEMOGS gives "The age of a person as of the extract date", while Snap-DOMINO gives "The age of a person as of the snap date", the day carried in SNAP_DATE. Age at a payment, a card or an assessment therefore has to be worked out from YEAR_OF_BIRTH and MONTH_OF_BIRTH against that event's own dates.
value_definition: Whole years, format N{NN} on the snapshot distribution, so a two- or three-digit integer with no fractional part and no code list.
limitation: It is not age at the event. Joining STATIC_DEMOGS to a payment history record and reading AGE gives the person's age at extraction, which can be many years after the payment, so an 'age at first payment' built this way is wrong by the length of the person's history. The two tables also disagree with each other by design, since one is anchored to the extract and the other to the snapshot day.
rationale: The registry publishes both PLIDA distributions and gives a different reference date for the same column name in each, which is the fact a user needs and the fplida description omitted.
evidence_quote: The age of a person as of the snap date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated 'Recipient age as of extract date' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and the description was wrong for the Snap-DOMINO occurrence, where age is measured at the snap date.

value_domain: Centrelink Integrated Activity Management reference number
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 614 'Recipient: Activity Management Reference (AMR) number, Code'
variable_description: The Centrelink work item that created or changed this medical conditions record. DSS defines it as a "Unique number/code allocated by Integrated Activity Management (IAM) within the context of a client record", and its role is as an audit trail: it ties a row back to the activity that produced it, and marks updates that are still provisional or logically deleted. On mcd_dtls it sits beside ASSMT_ID, so AMR answers which piece of Centrelink processing wrote the row while ASSMT_ID answers which medical assessment the condition came from.
value_definition: A number of up to four digits, format N[4], allocated within one client's record rather than across the population.
limitation: It is not a person key and not a national identifier, so the same value recurs in unrelated recipients' records and counting distinct values across the file counts nothing. It also carries no date, so it cannot be used to order events within a person's history.
rationale: The registry's data element for the AMR gives the definition, the four-digit format and the guidance that the number is an audit-trail link to the activity that generated the data, including flags for provisional and logically deleted records.
evidence_quote: Unique number/code allocated by Integrated Activity Management (IAM) within the context of a client record.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Activity management reference' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, leaving a reader with no idea that the number is an internal audit key rather than an identifier they could join on.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_APPR_TRN_EXT (PLIDA), column apt_end_date
variable_description: The day the apprenticeship or traineeship recorded on this row stopped, as DSS puts it the "End date of an apprentice or traineeship event". The table carries three dates that do different jobs: APT_START_DATE and this column bound the event as it actually ran, while APT_STDNT_END_DATE is the end that was expected when it started. Comparing the actual end against the expected end is what identifies an early exit, and EUEA_ID groups the rows belonging to one education episode.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, open domain, empty while the apprenticeship is still running.
limitation: An end date is not evidence of completion. Cancellation, suspension and a transfer to a different employer all close an event, and this table carries no completion flag, so a filled end date on its own cannot separate an apprentice who finished from one who withdrew.
rationale: The registry publishes the PLIDA distribution of the apprenticeship and traineeship table with a verbatim definition for each column, which is what distinguishes the actual end date from the expected one.
evidence_quote: End date of an apprentice or traineeship event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Apprenticeship end date' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave a reader no way to tell it apart from APT_STDNT_END_DATE on the same row.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_APPR_TRN_EXT (PLIDA), column apt_start_date
variable_description: The day the apprenticeship or traineeship on this row began, given by DSS as the "Start date of an apprentice or traineeship event". Only training that touched a Centrelink payment is here, because the table exists to support student and youth payment assessment, so this is not a start date for apprentices in general and cannot be read as a national commencements series. PERIOD_START_DATE sitting beside it is the reporting period the record was extracted in, not the training start, and TYPE_CODE gives the field of education.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form. The domain is open and there is no code list.
limitation: The date belongs to a training event, not to a person's whole apprenticeship. An apprentice who changes employer part-way through generates a fresh event with a new start date, so counting start dates overstates how many apprenticeships were begun, and EUEA_ID has to be used to collapse the events into episodes.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the apprenticeship table defines each column and shows the episode identifier and the reporting period columns that qualify this date.
evidence_quote: Start date of an apprentice or traineeship event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the variable name as 'Apprenticeship start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_APPR_TRN_EXT (PLIDA), column apt_stdnt_end_date
variable_description: The date the apprenticeship or traineeship was expected to finish, which DSS gives as the "Expected end date of an apprentice or traineeship". It is the planned end rather than the observed one, and APT_END_DATE holds the day the event actually stopped. The gap between the two is the usable signal in this table, because a training contract that ends well short of its expected end is the mark of a non-completion, and Centrelink uses the expected end to decide how long a student payment can continue.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, set when the apprenticeship is registered and revised when the contract changes.
limitation: An expected end date is a plan, not a course length. Because it is revised over the life of a contract, the value in the extract does not reliably measure nominal duration, and it says nothing at all about whether the qualification was awarded.
rationale: The registry defines this column as the expected end date and defines apt_end_date separately as the end of the event, which is the distinction the fplida description was missing.
evidence_quote: Expected end date of an apprentice or traineeship.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Apprenticeship student end date', which reads as a date for the student rather than a planned end, and it repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA), column assmt_id
variable_description: The medical assessment a recorded condition came from, described by DSS as "An assessment ID that links a medical condition to medical assessments". It is the key that ties the primary and secondary condition codes, the impairment rating and the work capacity hours on this row back to one assessment event. Because a person can hold several assessments over the years, each with its own value here, this column is what attributes a change in IMPRMT_RATE or CURR_CAPCTY_NUM to a reassessment rather than to a data correction.
value_definition: An opaque identifier with no published structure and no code list. Values are useful only for grouping rows that belong to one assessment.
limitation: It does not identify the assessor, the type of assessment, or whether the assessment supported a Disability Support Pension claim or an employment services referral; RFRL_RSN_CODE is what records why the assessment was sought. It also carries no date, so IMPRMT_VER_DATE has to be used to place the assessment in time.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the medical conditions table defines assmt_id verbatim and lists the impairment, capacity and referral columns that share the assessment it identifies.
evidence_quote: An assessment ID that links a medical condition to medical assessments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Assessment id' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing on the page explained what the identifier groups or why the same person holds several values.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_EMP_CONT_EXT (PLIDA), column avg_ind
variable_description: Whether the employment income on this row was averaged rather than reported for the days it was actually earned. DSS gives the column as a "Flag indicating employment income was derived by averaging". Centrelink averages earnings where a recipient's pay is irregular or reported over a longer interval, so a flagged row spreads one reported amount evenly across the period instead of recording day-by-day earnings. It qualifies EMP_DLY_INC_CONT and EMP_INC_CONT on the same row, and FREQ_CODE says how often the income was reported.
value_definition: A short indicator separating averaged income from income reported as earned. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code values.
limitation: It says the amount was smoothed but not by how much or over what window. A flagged row therefore cannot date when earnings actually occurred, so an analysis of week-to-week earnings volatility has to set these rows aside rather than treat them as observations of the underlying pay.
rationale: The registry publishes the PLIDA distribution of the continuous employment income table, defining avg_ind and the daily, stated and hours columns it qualifies.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating employment income was derived by averaging.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Income averaged indicator' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which told a reader nothing about what averaging does to the amounts beside it.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column birth_ctry_code
variable_description: The recipient's country of birth as Centrelink holds it, defined by DSS as "The country in which the person was born, as represented by a code". It is a static attribute of the person, carried unchanged on every snapshot row rather than observed at any event. Beside it on the Snap-DOMINO row sit LANG_CODE, the preferred spoken language, and INDIGENOUS, the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander status flag; static_demogs adds INTERPRETER_IND, whether an interpreter is needed.
value_definition: A two-character alphabetic code, format AA on the Snap-DOMINO distribution. It is a short DSS code set, not the four-digit ABS Standard Australian Classification of Countries used in Census and survey products; the registry lists a SACC-coded country of birth element separately for other DSS collections.
limitation: Country of birth is not visa status, year of arrival or citizenship, and DOMINO carries none of those, so this column cannot separate a recent arrival from someone who migrated as a child. It is recorded at claim time from what the person stated, and is empty for recipients who were never asked.
rationale: The registry gives the definition and the two-character format on the PLIDA distribution, and lists a distinct SACC 2016 country of birth data element for the Data Exchange, which shows the two collections do not share one classification.
evidence_quote: The country in which the person was born, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Recipient country of birth code' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no hint that the codes are not the ABS classification a user would reach for.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_BUS_EXT (PLIDA), column bus_dly_ass_non_prmy_prdct
variable_description: Daily income Centrelink attributed to the recipient's business assets outside primary production, defined by DSS as "Daily income from non-primary production business assets". It is one of five streams the business income table splits out on a single row: earned, unearned, real estate, primary production assets and non-primary production assets. The split exists because the income test treats these differently, and PERIOD_START_DATE to PERIOD_END_DATE gives the span the daily rate applies over.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day, not a fortnightly or annual total. It is the amount assessed under the social security income test, so it is already net of the deductions those rules allow.
limitation: This is not accounting profit and will not reconcile to what the business reported to the ATO, because Centrelink assesses business income under its own rules and on its own timing. A nil value means nothing was assessed for the period rather than that the assets earned nothing.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the business income table defines each of the five income columns verbatim and shows they sit on one row bounded by a reporting period.
evidence_quote: Daily income from non-primary production business assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Business daily income from non-primary product assets' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not say that the amount is a daily assessed rate rather than a reported figure.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_BUS_EXT (PLIDA), column bus_dly_ass_prmy_prdct
variable_description: Daily income Centrelink attributed to the recipient's primary production business assets, which DSS defines as "Daily income from primary production business assets" and which covers farming, fishing and forestry. It is kept apart from the non-primary production figure because primary producers are subject to their own averaging and drought concessions in the income test, so the two should not be merged without thought. The amount applies across the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day over the reporting period, assessed under the social security income test rather than reported as accounting income.
limitation: It does not identify the business, the commodity or the holding, and no ABN appears on this table, so a farm here cannot be matched to its BLADE or tax records. A zero cannot be read as a failed season either, since assessment can be deferred or suspended while circumstances are reviewed.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution defines this column and its non-primary production counterpart, and lists every column on the table, which shows no business identifier is carried.
evidence_quote: Daily income from primary production business assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Business daily income from primary product assets' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what primary production means here or why it is separated out.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_BUS_EXT (PLIDA), column bus_dly_inc_earn
variable_description: The part of a recipient's business income that Centrelink treated as earned, given by DSS as "Daily income earned from business activities/assets". The earned and unearned split drives the income test, because earned income attracts concessions such as the working credit and the income free area that unearned income does not, so the two columns record a rules distinction rather than an accounting one. BUS_DLY_INC_UNEARN on the same row carries the other side of the split.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day across the reporting period, as assessed under the income test.
limitation: Earned business income is not wages and cannot be turned into an hourly rate: this table has no hours column, unlike inc_emp_cont, which carries EMP_INC_CONT_HRS. A self-employed recipient's labour input is therefore invisible here.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution defines the earned and unearned business income columns and lists the full column set, which shows no hours field on this table.
evidence_quote: Daily income earned from business activities/assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Business daily income earned' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the earned and unearned pair looked like two unexplained amounts rather than an income test distinction.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_BUS_EXT (PLIDA), column bus_dly_inc_real_estate
variable_description: Daily income Centrelink attributed to the recipient's real estate business assets, defined by DSS as "Daily income from real estate business assets" and most often rent from property held in a business structure. BUS_DLY_INC_REAL_ESTATE_CODE beside it records the "Source of real estate income evaluation", which is what separates a valuation from a self-assessment. Both apply across the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day, assessed under the income test rather than taken from a rental statement.
limitation: It counts income, not property. No address, property count or valuation appears, so this column cannot identify landlords or be matched to the ATO rental property schedule, where the ARID does identify the dwelling. Rental income held outside a business structure is assessed elsewhere and does not appear here.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution defines the real estate income column and its companion evaluation source code, and lists every column on the table.
evidence_quote: Daily income from real estate business assets.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Business daily income from real estate' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention the evaluation source code that qualifies the amount.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_BUS_EXT (PLIDA), column bus_dly_inc_unearn
variable_description: The part of a recipient's business income that Centrelink treated as unearned, which DSS describes as "Daily business income received from other sources (interest etc.)". Unearned income is assessed at full rate under the income test with none of the working credit concessions that apply to earned income, so a dollar recorded here reduces a payment differently from a dollar in BUS_DLY_INC_EARN. The two columns together give the recipient's assessed business income for the period.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day over the reporting period, assessed under the income test.
limitation: It does not break down what the unearned income was: interest, dividends and trust distributions all fall in together, with no component detail anywhere on the table. Personal investment income held outside the business is assessed in other DOMINO income tables and is not part of this figure.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution defines the unearned business income column verbatim, including the examples the department itself gives.
evidence_quote: Daily business income received from other sources (interest etc.)
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried 'Business daily unearned income' and the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave no examples of what counts as unearned.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column card_any_health_care
variable_description: Whether the person held any kind of Health Care Card on the snapshot date. DSS names the four types it rolls up: the automatic issue card, the ex-Carer Allowance card, the foster child card and the low income card, which are the same four carried individually as CARD_HEALTH_CARE_AUTO, _ECH, _FST and _LOW_INC. It is true when any of those is true and excludes the Pensioner Concession Card and the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which have their own flags and their own broader concessions.
value_definition: A boolean flag evaluated at SNAP_DATE rather than over a period, so it describes a single day of the year.
limitation: It cannot tell you which card was held, for how long, or whether the card was still pending rather than active. A person who held a card for one day of the year is indistinguishable from one who held a card all year, because the flag is read on the snapshot day alone.
rationale: The registry's Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution defines the column as a boolean and lists the four health care card types it covers, and it carries the four individual card flags as separate columns.
evidence_quote: Indicates that the card holder with any of these health care cards
supersedes_rationale: The entry pasted the custodian's run-on wording, which lists the four card types without punctuation, and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 458 'Card: Concession Card, Number of Listed Children'
variable_description: The largest number of children listed on any one of the person's concession cards on the snapshot date. DSS defines it as "The maximum number of children listed on a concession card held by the card holder", so for a person holding several cards it reports the biggest single child list rather than the total across cards. It is the Snap-DOMINO counterpart of EXT_DOM_CHILD_ID_LIST_COUNT on the concession card detail tables, where the individual children are identified.
value_definition: A whole number, format {NNNN}N with a maximum of five characters, and 0 supplied as the default where no children are listed.
limitation: Children listed on a card are not children in the household and not dependants for payment purposes. A child can be listed on both parents' cards and so counted twice across the file, while a dependent young person above the listing age is left out entirely, so this is not a count of the person's children.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the format and the default value, and the Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution binds the column to it.
evidence_quote: The maximum number of children listed on a concession card held by the card holder
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'The total number of children listed on a concession card.', which is wrong in the way that matters: the value is a maximum across cards, not a total, and the generic no-value-list sentence stood as both definition and limitation.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 108787 'Card: Concession Card Count'
variable_description: How many concession cards the person held on the snapshot date, across all types. DSS defines it as the "total count of concession cards held by the card holder", so someone holding both a Pensioner Concession Card and a Health Care Card counts two. CARD_ANY is the yes-or-no version of the same fact, and the individual CARD_PENSION and CARD_HEALTH_CARE_* flags say which types make up the count.
value_definition: An integer, format N(8), with 0 as the default where no card is held.
limitation: It counts cards, not concessions or their value. A second card usually adds little, because the Pensioner Concession Card already carries the wider set of Commonwealth concessions, so a count of two does not mean twice the benefit. Only cards current on SNAP_DATE are counted, so a card that lapsed the week before is invisible.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the integer format and the zero default, and the Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution binds the column to it.
evidence_quote: indicates the total count of concession cards held by the card holder
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so nothing said the count is taken on a single snapshot day.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column card_end_date
variable_description: The day the concession card on this row expires, which DSS states as "The date on which a concession card expires, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It is the end of the card's usable life rather than the end of the entitlement behind it: END_REASON_CODE says why the card stopped and PERIOD_END_DATE bounds the reporting period the row was extracted in. With CARD_START_DATE it gives the span over which the card could be presented for a concession.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form. Cards are issued for a fixed term, so the value usually sits a set interval after CARD_START_DATE rather than being driven by the recipient's circumstances.
limitation: Expiry is not loss of eligibility. Cards are reissued automatically while entitlement continues, so a person with unbroken eligibility shows a run of consecutive card rows with expiry dates in the middle of it, and treating each expiry as an exit from concession coverage manufactures churn that never happened.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines the column as the card's expiry and carries a separate end reason code, which shows expiry and cessation are recorded distinctly.
evidence_quote: The date on which a concession card expires, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Concession card end date' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and left the reader to assume the date marks the end of eligibility rather than the end of a card term.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column card_health_care_auto
variable_description: Whether the person held an automatically issued Health Care Card on the snapshot date. DSS notes these cards "are automatically issued to recipients of certain payments", so the card follows the payment rather than being claimed, and the flag sits close to being a marker of JobSeeker, Parenting Payment or a similar allowance. CARD_HEALTH_CARE_LOW_INC covers the separately claimed low income card, and CARD_PENSION the pensioner card that some payments attract instead.
value_definition: A boolean flag evaluated at SNAP_DATE, one value per person per snapshot row.
limitation: It does not name the payment that triggered the card; ISP_TYPE_CODE on the same row is what does that. Nor can it stand in for payment receipt, because several payments carry a Pensioner Concession Card rather than a Health Care Card, and those recipients show false here while still being on income support.
rationale: The registry's Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution defines this column as a boolean and states that the card is issued automatically with certain payments, and the same distribution carries the income support payment type code.
evidence_quote: They are automatically issued to recipients of certain payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pasted the custodian's two-sentence gloss on Health Care Cards in general and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that this particular flag is the automatic card only.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column card_health_care_low_inc
variable_description: Whether the person held a Low Income Health Care Card on the snapshot date. DSS records that "People with income below certain levels can claim a Health Care Card", with thresholds set on average weekly gross income over the eight weeks before the claim and varying by partner status and number of dependent children. Unlike the automatic card, this one is claimed rather than issued with a payment, which makes it the flag that picks up low-income people outside the income support system.
value_definition: A boolean flag evaluated at SNAP_DATE. The dollar thresholds quoted in the DSS metadata are the rates current when the item was documented and are indexed each year, so they date the definition rather than describing the whole series.
limitation: The test is on the eight weeks before the claim, not on income at the snapshot date, so holding the card is evidence of past low income and not of current low income. A person whose earnings recovered after claiming keeps the card until the next review, which means the flag lags the circumstance it stands for.
rationale: The registry's Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution defines the column as a boolean and reproduces the income test and the threshold table that governs the card.
evidence_quote: People with income below certain levels can claim a Health Care Card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pasted the custodian's threshold table as its description, which reads as a rate schedule rather than a definition of the column, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column card_health_care_senior
variable_description: Whether the person held a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card on the snapshot date. DSS describes the card as "targeted at self-funded retirees of Age Pension age who do not receive Age Pension because of assets or income levels", which makes this the one flag in Snap-DOMINO that marks a group otherwise nearly absent from the file: people of pension age with no income support record. Holders may also receive the Energy Supplement, which turns up as a payment component in the payment history tables.
value_definition: A boolean flag evaluated at SNAP_DATE, held on the person's snapshot row.
limitation: It is not a measure of wealth or of retirement. The card is income tested but not assets tested, so a person with large assets and low drawn income holds it while a part-pensioner with modest assets does not, and a self-funded retiree who never claimed the card shows false despite meeting the criteria.
rationale: The registry's Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution defines the column as a boolean and states who the card targets and why they are not on the Age Pension.
evidence_quote: The Commonwealth Seniors Health Card is targeted at self-funded retirees of Age Pension age who do not receive Age Pension because of assets or income levels.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pasted the custodian's description of the card scheme and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the column is a boolean read on a single day.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column card_issue_date
variable_description: The day the concession card on this row was produced and sent, which DSS gives as "The date on which a concession card is issued" and which is not the day the card becomes usable. CARD_START_DATE carries that, and ACTION_DATE the day the decision was processed, so the three columns separate the decision, the production and the entitlement period. REASON_CODE says why an issue or reissue was requested, including replacement of a lost card.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form. Reissues create new issue dates against a continuing entitlement, so the dates recur through a person's history at roughly the card's term length.
limitation: The issue date does not date the start of concession entitlement, and using it that way understates coverage, because a replacement card issued mid-term produces an issue date with no change in entitlement behind it. It also cannot distinguish a first grant from a routine reissue without REASON_CODE.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines the issue date and separately defines the start date as when the card is able to be used, plus a reason code for issue and reissue.
evidence_quote: The date on which a concession card is issued.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Concession card issue date' with the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and gave a reader no way to choose between the issue, start and action dates on the same row.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA), column card_pension
variable_description: Whether the person held a Pensioner Concession Card on the snapshot date. DSS notes the card "provides access to more Australian Government concessions than those offered to other cardholders, including subsidised hearing assessments and hearing rehabilitation", so it sits above the Health Care Card in the concession hierarchy. It is issued automatically to pensioners and, in some circumstances, to recipients of other payments, which makes it a close but imperfect marker of Age Pension, Disability Support Pension or Carer Payment receipt.
value_definition: A boolean flag evaluated at SNAP_DATE, one value per snapshot row.
limitation: The flag does not say which payment brought the card, and because non-pension recipients hold it in defined circumstances it cannot substitute for pension receipt; ISP_TYPE_CODE is the column that names the payment. Recipients who keep the card after a payment ends, under the extended entitlement rules, also still show true.
rationale: The registry's Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution defines the column as a boolean and describes both the automatic issue to pensioners and the wider concession set the card carries.
evidence_quote: It provides access to more Australian Government concessions than those offered to other cardholders, including subsidised hearing assessments and hearing rehabilitation.
supersedes_rationale: The entry pasted the custodian's description of the card scheme and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both the definition and the limitation, without noting that the flag is not a proxy for pension receipt.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column card_postcode
variable_description: The postcode printed on the concession card, which DSS defines as "The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address" and which is the address Centrelink held for the cardholder when the card was made. CARD_STATE_CODE gives the state on the same card. Because the postcode is captured once per card, a run of card rows gives a coarse address history that can be checked against the finer location tables, loc_dtls and loc_derived.
value_definition: A four-digit Australian postcode. Postcodes are Australia Post delivery areas rather than statistical areas, so they do not nest inside ABS geography and cannot be aggregated cleanly to SA2 or LGA.
limitation: A postcode is a mail delivery area, not a place of residence: post office box ranges cover no population, and a cardholder who gives a postal address will show a postcode where nobody lives. The value also freezes when the card is made, so it lags a move by up to the card's term.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines the postcode column verbatim and pairs it with the card state code, and the DOMINO location tables carry the address geography separately.
evidence_quote: The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Postcode listed on concession card' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on the page warning that a card postcode can be a postal address rather than a residence.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column card_start_date
variable_description: The day the concession card first becomes usable, which DSS glosses as the date a card "starts (i.e. is able to be used)". With CARD_END_DATE it bounds the window in which a cardholder could claim concessions, and that pair is the one to use for coverage, since ACTION_DATE and CARD_ISSUE_DATE are administrative and can fall either side of it. CONCESSION and ENT_TYPE on the same row say what kind of card and entitlement the window belongs to.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, marking the first day the card can be presented.
limitation: The start of a card is not the start of eligibility, because a card can be backdated to a determination or delayed after one. Consecutive card records also overlap where a card is replaced before its expiry, so adding up start-to-end spans double counts days of coverage rather than measuring them.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines this column as the date the card can be used, which distinguishes it from the issue and action dates defined on the same page.
evidence_quote: The date on which a concession card starts (i.e. is able to be used), expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Concession card start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without the parenthetical that makes this the usable-from date rather than another administrative stamp.

value_domain: State or territory of card issue, code
value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column card_state_code
variable_description: The state or territory the concession card was issued in, held as a code and defined by DSS as "The state or territory in which a concession card is issued". It records where Centrelink processed and issued the card, not where the holder lives, though for most cardholders the two agree; CARD_POSTCODE on the same row is the finer address geography. State matters for concession cards because much of a card's practical value — transport fares, council rates, vehicle registration — is set by state and territory governments rather than the Commonwealth.
value_definition: A short code for one of the eight states and territories. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code list, so a mapping to the ABS state codes used in the location tables has to be established from the data rather than assumed.
limitation: It is not the cardholder's state of residence. A card issued while the person was living interstate, or produced by a processing centre in another state, keeps the issuing state, so this column should not be used as a geography variable when loc_dtls carries the address state directly.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines the column as the state of issue rather than of residence, and the DOMINO location tables carry an address state separately.
evidence_quote: The state or territory in which a concession card is issued.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Concession card state code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and a reader would reasonably have taken the field for the holder's state of residence.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_CDEP_EXT (PLIDA), column cdep_dly_inc
variable_description: Daily wages a recipient received for taking part in the Community Development Employment Projects scheme, which DSS defines as "The daily income received by a recipient for participation in Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP)". CDEP was the Indigenous work-for-wages programme that ran from 1977 until it closed on 30 June 2015, and its income was assessed under separate rules, which is why it has its own table rather than sitting in inc_emp_cont. EMPLYR_ID identifies the CDEP organisation and CDEP_FREQ_CODE how often the income was reported.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day, applying across the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE.
limitation: An empty column in later years means the programme no longer existed, not that the person stopped working: participants moved to the Remote Jobs and Communities Program and then the Community Development Programme, whose activity is recorded elsewhere. The column also does not mark the recipient as Indigenous, since DOMINO holds Indigenous status separately and CDEP had non-Indigenous participants in some communities.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the CDEP income table gives the definition, the employer identifier and the frequency code that qualify the amount. The programme's closure date is well documented in Australian Indigenous employment policy histories.
evidence_quote: The daily income received by a recipient for participation in Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Cdep daily income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, expanding neither the acronym nor the reason the series stops.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution INC_CDEP_OTHER_EXT (PLIDA), column cdep_dly_inc_other
variable_description: Daily Community Development Employment Projects income of a kind other than the participant's basic CDEP wage, defined by DSS as "Other daily income received by a client for participation in Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP)". It lives in its own table, inc_cdep_other, rather than as a second column beside CDEP_DLY_INC, so a participant with both kinds of income has rows in two tables for the same period and the amounts must be added to get total CDEP income. Both tables carry EMPLYR_ID and CDEP_FREQ_CODE in the same form.
value_definition: An Australian dollar amount expressed as a rate per day over the reporting period, with the same shape and frequency coding as the main CDEP income column.
limitation: The registry does not say what 'other' covers, so the split from the basic CDEP wage cannot be given a substantive reading; treating the two tables as one income total is safer than interpreting the difference. As with the main column, the series ends when CDEP closed in 2015.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the CDEP other income table gives the verbatim definition and shows the table carries the same employer and frequency columns as the main CDEP table.
evidence_quote: Other daily income received by a client for participation in Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Cdep other daily income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without noting that this sits in a separate table from the main CDEP income.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 108685 'Address: Commonwealth Electoral Division, Code (ASGS 2022) NNN'
variable_description: The federal electorate covering the recipient's address on the snapshot date, which DSS defines as "The Commonwealth electoral division that a given address is located within, as represented by a code". It is one of a set of geographies derived from that one address on the Snap-DOMINO row, alongside MESHBLOCK, SA2, SA3, SA4, LGA, GCCSA, POSTCODE and STATE. It is the only one of them aligned to political rather than statistical boundaries, which is what makes it the column to use for reporting welfare receipt by electorate.
value_definition: A three-digit numeric code, format N(3), from the ASGS 2022 Commonwealth Electoral Division classification, which the ABS builds from Australian Electoral Commission boundaries.
limitation: Electoral boundaries are redistributed between elections while the column is coded to a single ASGS edition, so a time series by division silently mixes areas whose boundaries moved. It encodes the division only, not the sitting member or party, and it describes the address Centrelink held rather than where the person is enrolled to vote.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the three-digit format and the ASGS 2022 classification behind it, and the Snap-DOMINO PLIDA distribution binds the ced column to that element.
evidence_quote: The Commonwealth electoral division that a given address is located within, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's one-line description and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which classification or edition the codes come from.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA), column child_id
variable_description: Identifies a child listed on the cardholder's concession card, which is how a card's concessions extend to dependants. DSS defines it as "A numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies the child(ren) of a recipient on a concession card". Four sibling columns separate the other kinds of listed person: EXT_DOM_FST_CHILD_ID a foster child, EXT_DOM_OTH_CHILD_ID an other child, EXT_DOM_CDA_CHILD_ID a child attracting Carer Allowance and EXT_DOM_DEP_CUSTOMER_ID a dependent customer, with EXT_DOM_CHILD_ID_LIST_COUNT giving the maximum number of children listed on a card.
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned by Centrelink. The related child identifiers on the same table are described as randomised, so the values carry no information about the child and serve only to match rows.
limitation: It is not the synthetic MADIP person identifier that links DOMINO to the rest of PLIDA, so a listed child cannot be followed into their own records from this column. It also cannot establish parentage: a child is listed because of a care arrangement, which is not the same as a biological or legal relationship.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the health care card table defines child_id verbatim and lists the four sibling identifiers and the list count that qualify it, alongside synthetic_aeuid as the separate person key.
evidence_quote: A numeric sequence of characters assigned by Centrelink that identifies the child(ren) of a recipient on a concession card.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Child id' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, leaving open the far more damaging reading that the identifier links to the child's own PLIDA records.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_FTB_EXT (PLIDA), column cmpltn_date
variable_description: The day a course of study was completed, on the education records Centrelink keeps for Family Tax Benefit purposes: DSS defines it as "The date on which a recipient's course of study is completed, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". The row describes one course, with COURSE_LVL, COURSE_TYPE and INST_TYPE saying what was studied and where, and STDNT_START_DATE and STDNT_END_DATE bounding participation. Study is captured at all because Family Tax Benefit Part A for a child aged 16 or over depends on full-time study continuing.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form, present only where a course was completed, so it is empty for study still under way and for study abandoned.
limitation: A completion date is not a qualification and not a school-leaving date; it closes one course, so a student who finishes several has several dates. The registry's own column definitions on this table shift between the Family Tax Benefit recipient and the recipient's child, so which person the date belongs to should be checked against SYNTHETIC_AEUID before the dates are used.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution of the education Family Tax Benefit table defines every column, and the wording of course_lvl and cmpltn_y12_ind refers to the recipient's child while cmpltn_ind refers to the recipient, which is the ambiguity worth flagging.
evidence_quote: The date on which a recipient's course of study is completed, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Completion date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to say what was completed or why Centrelink holds education records at all.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_FTB_EXT (PLIDA), column cmpltn_ind
variable_description: Whether the course of study on this row was completed, which DSS states as "Indicates whether a recipient has completed their course of study". CMPLTN_DATE carries the day it happened and STDNT_PRTCPN_STS the current participation status, so this flag is the summary of an education episode those columns bracket. The table exists to support Family Tax Benefit assessment, where continued payment for a child aged 16 or over turns on study.
value_definition: An indicator flag separating completed from not completed. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code values.
limitation: A 'not completed' value covers both study still under way and study abandoned, which are quite different states; STDNT_PRTCPN_STS is the column that separates them. The flag also only sees courses reported to Centrelink, so a child whose family left the payment system mid-course simply stops appearing rather than being recorded as incomplete.
rationale: The registry's PLIDA distribution defines the completion indicator, the completion date and the student participation status as three distinct columns, which is what shows the flag cannot separate ongoing from abandoned study.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether a recipient has completed their course of study.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Completion indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what is completed or how an unfinished course looks.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution EDU_FTB_EXT (PLIDA), column cmpltn_y12_ind
variable_description: Whether a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child has completed Year 12, which DSS states in exactly those terms: "Indicates whether a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child has completed year 12". It is the only column in this table that reports an attainment level rather than a course event, which makes it the closest thing DOMINO holds to a school completion measure for children in payment-receiving families. CMPLTN_IND beside it refers to a course of study rather than to schooling.
value_definition: An indicator flag on the education record; the PLIDA distribution does not publish its code values.
limitation: It sees Year 12 completion only for children whose family claimed Family Tax Benefit and reported study, so it is not a population completion rate and skews toward lower-income families. A Year 12 equivalent qualification, such as a Certificate III, does not set the flag, so vocational pathways are recorded as non-completion.
rationale: The registry defines this column as Year 12 completion for the recipient's child and defines the general course completion indicator separately, which is the distinction the fplida description collapsed.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child has completed year 12.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Year 12 completion indicator', was tagged with a date topic rather than an education one, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, never saying whose Year 12 completion is recorded.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 388 'Payment: Component daily amount, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: The daily dollar value of one component of a payment, which is the unit DOMINO records payments in: DSS defines it as "The amount of a component type that is paid to an allocation of the recipient's payment". A recipient's fortnightly payment is built from components — the basic rate, rent assistance, the pension supplement, the energy supplement and so on — and each gets its own row, with CMPNT_TYPE naming the component and BEN_TYPE naming the payment it belongs to. Reconstructing what a person actually received means summing this column over components and over the days in each period, across the twenty-five payment history tables that carry it.
value_definition: A decimal Australian dollar amount, format N[9].NN, expressed per day rather than per fortnight, and applying across the span from PERIOD_START_DATE to PERIOD_END_DATE.
limitation: A single row is never a person's payment, and reading one component as the payment amount, or the daily figure as a fortnightly one, understates income by a factor that changes with the number of components and the length of the period. The column also holds entitlement as assessed, so debts, deductions, advances and third-party payments do not net off against it and the figure is not money transferred.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the decimal format and the Australian currency unit, and the PYH_COMBINED_DIS PLIDA distribution shows the component type, benefit type and period columns that qualify each amount.
evidence_quote: The amount of a component type that is paid to an allocation of the recipient's payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Component daily amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, on the most-used variable in DOMINO, where the daily-and-per-component shape is exactly what a reader gets wrong.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 385 'Payment: Payment component identifier, ID text'
variable_description: Identifies the individual item being paid within a payment component, and it is what holds a payment record together: DSS defines it as "The unique identifier for an item being paid under the given component" and says it links a gross payment allocation group to its matching rate component allocation group. On the payment history tables it groups the rows that make up one allocation, so CMPNT_DLY_AMT values sharing a value belong together and should be summed rather than treated as alternatives.
value_definition: A string in the form AAN{NNN}: a two-character system code followed by a number, assigned sequentially by the payment details update module.
limitation: The identifier is unique only within one record, not across recipients or across time, so it cannot be counted, joined on by itself, or used to trace a payment between tables. Two rows carrying the same value in different people's records are unrelated, which is the trap a reader falls into when treating it as a payment key.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the AAN{NNN} format and the explicit guidance that the identifier is unique only within a specific record.
evidence_quote: The unique identifier for an item being paid under the given component.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Payment component id' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the identifier is record-local and not a key that can be joined across the payment history tables.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA), column cntry_cde
variable_description: The country a recipient usually lives in, on the derived location table, which DSS defines as "The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code". Its practical job on loc_derived is to mark the rows where the Australian geography is empty because the address is overseas: MB_ASGS_2021, SA1_ASGS_2021, SA2_ASGS_2021, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021 have nothing to code for an address abroad, and this column is what separates that case from a missing address. ADDR_PRTY ranks competing addresses for the same day.
value_definition: A code for the country of usual residence. loc_dtls carries the same concept as CTRY_CODE and the registry gives both an identical definition, so the two are the derived and raw versions of one field rather than different measures.
limitation: Country of usual residence is not country of birth — BIRTH_CTRY_CODE holds that — and it is not a travel record: a recipient temporarily overseas keeps their Australian address unless Centrelink records a change of usual residence, so short absences leave no trace. The column also does not date a move on its own; START_DATE and END_DATE bound the episode.
rationale: The registry's LOC_DERIVED PLIDA distribution defines cntry_cde verbatim and lists the ASGS geography columns beside it that only apply to Australian addresses.
evidence_quote: The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Country of residence', was tagged social security rather than geography, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying what the column does for overseas addresses.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA), column ctry_code
variable_description: The country of an address held for the recipient on the raw location detail table, defined by DSS as "The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code". On loc_dtls it qualifies the Australian geography columns beside it — MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, STATE and POSTCODE — which have nothing to hold for an overseas address, while ADDR_TYPE_CODE says whether the address is residential, postal or something else. The same column appears on loc_pos_temp_term_dtls, the temporary and terminated postal address table, where overseas values are more common.
value_definition: A country code with the same definition the derived location table gives to CNTRY_CDE. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code list.
limitation: It describes the address on the row, not the person's residency status, so it cannot be used to identify migrants, temporary residents or recipients being paid overseas under portability rules. Because ADDR_PRTY ranks competing addresses, a person can hold several current rows with different countries, so the priority column has to be applied earlier in this one is read.
rationale: The registry's LOC_DTLS_EXT PLIDA distribution defines ctry_code verbatim, lists the address priority and address type columns that qualify it, and gives the same definition to cntry_cde on the derived table.
evidence_quote: The country of usual residence of a person, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address country' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not connect the column to the address priority ranking that decides which row applies.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 54225 'Recipient: Current capacity hours, Total number'
variable_description: How many hours a week the recipient is currently assessed as able to work, which DSS defines as "The number of current capacity in hours a recipient is able to work in a week". This number is what the partial capacity to work rules and the Disability Support Pension assessment turn on, so it decides mutual obligation requirements as much as it describes health. Three columns qualify it on the same row: WITH_INTRVN_NUM gives capacity if intervention or support were provided, TEMP_REDN_CAP_HRS_NUM a temporary reduction, and INCAP_WK_WRK_HRS the hours the issuing doctor considers the client able to work, with ASSMT_ID keying the assessment they all came from.
value_definition: Whole hours per week, format N(2), so values from 0 to 99, with a full stop used as the missing value indicator.
limitation: It is an assessed capacity, not observed work. A recipient assessed at 15 hours may be working none of them or more than them, and inc_emp_cont is where actual earnings and hours sit, so this column measures what an assessment concluded rather than labour supply. The value is also frozen at the assessment and stays put until a reassessment, so it can be years old on any given row.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition, the two-digit format, the hours-per-week unit and the full stop as the missing value, and the MCD_DTLS_EXT PLIDA distribution shows the related capacity and incapacity columns.
evidence_quote: The number of current capacity in hours a recipient is able to work in a week.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Current work capacity number' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell the units were hours per week or that a full stop means missing.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, data element 467 'Person: Date of death, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the recipient died, as Centrelink's records hold it, defined by DSS as "The date upon which a person ceases to live, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It sits on the static demographics table because it is an attribute of the person rather than an event, and it exists for an administrative reason: a death stops payments and starts bereavement provisions. DEATH_IND beside it flags that the person is recorded as deceased, and the two disagree wherever a death is known but not dated.
value_definition: A calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form. Other DOMINO releases carry only month of death and year of death as separate columns, so the precision available depends on which version of the static demographics table is in hand.
limitation: This is not a death registration and it is not complete: only deaths that came to Centrelink's attention are here, so a former recipient who died years after leaving the payment system has no date. The PLIDA deaths module, built from state and territory registrations, is the source for mortality; this column is best used to explain why a payment stopped.
rationale: The registry's data element gives the definition and the date format, and its STATIC_DEMOGS PLIDA distribution carries month and year of death as separate columns, which is why the precision caveat is worth stating.
evidence_quote: The date upon which a person ceases to live, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Recipient date of death' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing to warn that the column only sees deaths the payment system learned about.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry, distribution STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA), column death_ind
variable_description: Flags that Centrelink's records show the recipient as deceased, defined by DSS in plain terms as "The indicator represents the death of a person". It is a static attribute of the person rather than a dated event, and DATE_OF_DEATH carries the date where one is held, so a flag set without a date is possible. Snap-DOMINO carries the same concept on its snapshot rows under the name DEATH_INDICATOR.
value_definition: An indicator flag on the person's demographic record. The PLIDA distribution does not publish the code values.
limitation: It shows what the payment system knows, not whether the person is alive. Deaths of people who left income support years earlier often never reach Centrelink, so a false value cannot be read as survival, and this flag should not be used to censor a longitudinal analysis in place of the PLIDA deaths data built from registrations.
rationale: The registry's STATIC_DEMOGS PLIDA distribution defines the column verbatim and shows it sits with the date, month and year of death columns on the person-level demographics table.
evidence_quote: The indicator represents the death of a person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Death indicator', was tagged social security, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the flag reflects administrative knowledge rather than vital status.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Person: Death, Indicator X(6)" (item 84486), bound to snap_domino_beta.death_indicator
variable_description: Whether Centrelink had recorded the person as deceased by the time the Snap-DOMINO extract was drawn. Snap-DOMINO holds one row per person per snapshot, so the flag is a property of the extract rather than of SNAP_DATE, and it is the only mortality information on the table. The static demographics table carries the fuller account: DEATH_IND with DATE_OF_DEATH, which is what you need to close off a person's exposure period rather than merely drop them.
value_definition: A single letter held in a six-character field: Y where a death has been recorded. DSS treats N as a supplementary default value rather than a positive statement, so N carries less information than Y does.
limitation: A recorded death is a death Centrelink learned about, usually because a payment stopped or a family member notified the agency, so someone who died years after leaving the payment system can sit at N indefinitely. The flag also carries no date on this table, so it cannot say whether the death fell inside or outside the snapshot period, and a Y on an old snapshot does not tell you when the person died.
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT (PLIDA) binds death_indicator to "Person: Death, Indicator X(6)", whose value domain publishes Y as the only permissible value and N as the default.
evidence_quote: The indicator represents the death of a person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's one-line description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so a reader could not tell that N is a default rather than a confirmed survival.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) daily amount, Total Australian currency" (item 570), bound to inc_dfi.dfi_dly_dfisa_amt
variable_description: The daily rate of Defence Force Income Support Allowance the person was paid over the period the row covers, which DSS defines as the "Daily Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) amount paid to a recipient". DFISA topped up a veteran's social security payment to offset the effect of counting adjusted disability pension as income, so it only ever attached to another payment: BEN_TYPE_CODE on the same row names which one. The custodian's own description on this column reads "Department of Veterans Affairs daily income amount", which is the wording that belongs to DVA_DLY_INC in inc_dva; the two are different amounts on different tables.
value_definition: Australian dollars and cents at a daily rate, format N[9].NN in an eleven-character field, with 0 the default. It is a rate, not an instalment, so a period's total is the rate times the days between PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE.
limitation: It is neither the veteran's DVA disability pension nor the income support payment itself, only the allowance that compensated for one being counted against the other, so it understates a veteran's income by a wide margin. DFISA ceased on 1 January 2022, when adjusted disability income became exempt under the social security income test, so an absence of rows after that date is the payment ending rather than the person's circumstances changing.
rationale: INC_DFI_EXT (PLIDA) binds dfi_dly_dfisa_amt to DSS data element 570, which names the payment, gives the currency value domain and the N[9].NN format, and states that the amount is daily.
evidence_quote: Daily Defence Force Income Support Allowance (DFISA) amount paid to a recipient.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's description, which names the wrong agency's payment, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its definition and its limitation.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Event: Event period duration, Number" (item 405), bound to det_ben.durn_days
variable_description: How long the benefit determination on this row ran, which DSS defines as "The duration of a reporting episode expressed as number of days". The det_ben table holds one row per spell of a given payment, so the count spans PERIOD_START_DATE to PERIOD_END_DATE for the payment named in BEN_TYPE_CODE. BEN_STATUS says whether the spell was current or suspended, and END_RSN and END_RSN_CODE say why it closed, so the duration is only interpretable with those three columns beside it.
value_definition: A whole number of days in a five-digit field, format {NNNN}N, with 0 the default value.
limitation: It counts days on a determination, not days paid: a spell that ran at a nil rate or under suspension still contributes its days, so summing the column overstates time actually in receipt of money. Because each row is one payment's spell, a person who moved between payments has several rows whose durations overlap, and adding them gives more days than the person actually spent on income support.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient—impairment rating, NN[N] (%)" (item 616), bound to mcd_dtls.imprmt_rate

Twenty points is the level at which Disability Support Pension becomes reachable, which is why the distribution of this column clusters rather than spreading smoothly.
