value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108846, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap'
variable_description: Says whether the person was being paid an income support payment on the day the snapshot was taken. It is the flag that turns Snap DOMINO into a point-in-time count of income support recipients: SNAP_DATE gives the day, ISP_TYPE_CODE names which payment, ISP_BEN_STATUS gives its status, and ISP_PANEL_DAYS counts activity over the surrounding window rather than on the day alone. Read it beside the parallel FTBA_ON_SNAP, FTBB_ON_SNAP, RENT_ON_SNAP and SUP_ON_SNAP flags, which cover family payments, rent assistance and supplements on the same date.
value_definition: One character from the DSS yes/no/missing code domain: Y for received on the snapshot date, N for not. The domain admits a missing value as well, so a person with no income support record at all need not read as N.
limitation: A day is not a year. Someone paid for eleven months who happened to be off payment on the snapshot date reads as N, so the flag understates how many people touch income support over a period. It also carries no amount, and it does not separate a full-rate entitlement from one reduced to nil by the income test.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds the snap_domino_beta column isp_on_snap to the data element 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP on Snap', which publishes both the definition and the yes/no/missing value domain.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating Income Support Payment received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the data item list wording as its whole description and repeated 'The source metadata does not publish a finite value list.' as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what a snapshot flag measures or what it misses.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108845, 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days'
variable_description: Counts the days the person spent active on an income support payment across the panel window the snapshot belongs to, rather than on the snapshot day itself. It is what separates someone continuously on payment from someone who cycled on and off between snapshots, which the ISP_ON_SNAP flag cannot show. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bound the underlying spell, and DOMINO treats that spell as tolerating breaks of up to six weeks where the whole period runs under a year.
value_definition: An integer count of days in the registry's Count N(8) domain, with a published default of 0. Days are summed across income support payments of any type, so the total measures time on income support rather than time on one payment.
limitation: The total cannot tell you which payment the days belonged to, so a move from JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension inside the window collapses into a single number and only ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP separate them. Because 0 is the default, a genuine zero and a person with no income support history look identical.
rationale: The DSS Metadata Registry binds snap_domino_beta.isp_panel_days to 'Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Panel Days' and publishes its Count N(8) domain and its default of 0. The registry does not publish the length of the panel window, so that part of the description is read off the snapshot design rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on Income Support Payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's one-line wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so a reader could not tell what period the days were counted over.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 65366, 'Person: Preferred Spoken Language, Code XXX'
variable_description: The language the person prefers to speak, as recorded by Centrelink through the interpreter process. The DSS registry defines the field as "The code that represents the preferred spoken language of a customer who has requested the assistance of an interpreter", which is why it sits on static_demogs next to INTERPRETER_IND, the flag saying an interpreter was required. The same code is repeated on snap_domino_beta so that a snapshot of recipients can be cut by language without joining back to the demographics table.
value_definition: A three-character code from the DSS Language Code value domain, which is a Centrelink code set rather than the ABS Australian Standard Classification of Languages. The domain keeps retired codes marked do-not-use with end dates, so historical rows can carry codes no longer issued.
limitation: It is not a measure of English proficiency and not the main language spoken at home. Because it is populated through interpreter requests, a person who never asked for an interpreter can be blank or sit on a default regardless of what they speak, so counts of language groups from this column understate every community that manages without one. It is also not comparable with the Census language variable, which uses the ABS classification.
rationale: The registry maps both static_demogs.lang_code and snap_domino_beta.lang_code to the Preferred Spoken Language data element and publishes its definition, its three-character Language Code domain and the presence of deprecated codes.
evidence_quote: The code that represents the preferred spoken language of a customer who has requested the assistance of an interpreter.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Preferred spoken language code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing warned that the field is collected for interpreting rather than as a language statistic.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108856, 'Payment: Last Active ISP'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on at the close of the active payment spell that the snapshot falls in. With FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP it brackets the spell, so a row shows where a period on income support started and where it finished without joining to the payment history tables. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE give the dates of that spell, which DOMINO builds by stitching over breaks of up to six weeks.
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which runs to about a hundred values: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.
limitation: It names the last payment inside one stitched spell, not the last payment a person ever received, so a person who returns to income support after a longer break starts a new spell with its own closing payment. The column also gives no date for the change and no reason for it.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.last_active_isp to 'Payment: Last Active ISP' and gives its value domain as the DSS benefit type code, the same code set used by ISP_TYPE_CODE, PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP.
evidence_quote: Last payment in active Income Support Payment period
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, leaving the benefit type code set undocumented.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108688, 'Address: Local Government Area (ASGS 2021), Code NNNNN'
variable_description: The council area the person's address fell in on the snapshot date. The DSS registry defines it as "The designated region representing the whole geographical area of responsibility of an incorporated Local Government entity in which a given address is located, as represented by a code", which makes it the one geography on the snapshot table that matches an actual unit of government rather than a statistical area. It is the natural join for council-level service planning, while SA2, SA3 and SA4 on the same row are the ABS statistical alternatives.
value_definition: A code of up to five characters from the Local Government Areas (LGA) Code (2021) value domain, the ASGS code set for the council area a location belongs to.
limitation: LGAs do not nest inside the SA3 or SA4 codes beside them, and not every value is a council: where no incorporated local government exists the ABS codes the area as Unincorporated followed by the state or territory, which covers the whole of the Australian Capital Territory, northern South Australia and some other territories. Council amalgamations also retire and mint codes, so an LGA time series breaks where boundaries were redrawn.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.lga to the ASGS 2021 Local Government Area data element and publishes both the definition and the five-character 2021 LGA value domain.
evidence_quote: The designated region representing the whole geographical area of responsibility of an incorporated Local Government entity in which a given address is located, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Local government area' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no edition, no code width and no warning about unincorporated areas.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'
variable_description: The mesh block the person's address fell in, on the derived location table that holds one row per address episode. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", so this is the finest geography DOMINO publishes and everything else on the row aggregates from it. SA1_ASGS_2021, SA2_ASGS_2021, SA4_ASGS_2021 and STATE_ASGS_2021 are the same address at coarser levels, ARID_HASH_TRUNC identifies the address itself, and START_DATE and END_DATE bound the period the person was there.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS 2021 mesh block code, format N(11), whose leading digit is the state or territory. Mesh blocks nest exactly inside SA1s, so the SA1 column on the same row is a strict aggregation of this one.
limitation: The ABS designs a mesh block to hold roughly 30 to 60 dwellings, so it is a small area, not a dwelling or a household: two people sharing a code are neighbours and need not live together. Boundaries were redrawn between ASGS editions, so a 2021 code cannot be compared with the differently coded MESHBLOCK column in loc_dtls without a correspondence file.
rationale: The registry lists mb_asgs_2021 as a column of the LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) distribution and maps it to the ASGS 2021 Meshblock data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the N(11) value domain.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Mesh block coded to 2021 asgs' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no code width, no nesting rule and no warning that a mesh block is not a household.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 635, 'Recipient: Secondary medical condition identifier, ID number'
variable_description: Links a secondary medical condition record to the earlier record it replaced, so the condition history reads as a sequence of corrections rather than as a set of separate conditions. The DSS registry defines it as "An identifier that links a medical condition that has been overwritten". It sits on the medical conditions details table beside MED_SCNDRY_GRP, which names the condition group, and MED_SCNDRY_PERM, which records how lasting the condition was judged to be.
value_definition: A short number, one or two digits, from the registry's Secondary medical condition ID number domain, which auto-increments from 1. It distinguishes successive versions of a record rather than naming a condition.
limitation: The number carries no clinical meaning and cannot be used to identify or count conditions; MED_SCNDRY_GRP is the column that names what the condition was. Its absence means no record was overwritten, not that the person had no secondary condition, so treating a populated value as evidence of a second diagnosis double counts corrections as conditions.
rationale: The registry maps mcd_dtls.med_scndry_id to the Secondary medical condition identifier data element and publishes both its definition and the auto-incrementing N[N] domain. How the counter is scoped within a person's record is inferred from the auto-increment rule rather than stated.
evidence_quote: An identifier that links a medical condition that has been overwritten.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Secondary medical code identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader would reasonably have read it as a diagnosis code.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 230, 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code'
variable_description: Records how lasting the medical condition on this row was judged to be, which is the assessment that decides whether a condition can support a Disability Support Pension claim. The DSS registry binds the column to a data element defined as "The permanency of a recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code", and its five codes separate a permanent condition that has been diagnosed, treated and stabilised from one that is recurring or temporary. PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE bound the assessment, and IMPRMT_RATE on the same table carries the impairment rating that goes with it.
value_definition: One character from the DSS permanency code set: D for permanent, diagnosed, treated and stabilised; P for permanent, not diagnosed, treated and stabilised; M for permanent; R for recurring; T for temporary.
limitation: Permanency here is an administrative judgement made for payment purposes, not a clinical prognosis, and a T does not mean a doctor expected recovery. The registry also ties this column to the primary condition data element while the PLIDA data item list calls it secondary, so check it against MED_PRMY_GRP and MED_SCNDRY_GRP before assuming which condition it qualifies.
rationale: The MCD_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps med_scndry_perm to 'Recipient: Primary medical condition permanency, Code', which publishes the definition and the five-value permanency code domain. The naming mismatch between the registry and the data item list is unresolved, which is why the confidence is medium.
evidence_quote: The permanency of a recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Secondary medical code pemanent indicator' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, implying a yes-or-no flag when the domain has five graded codes.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108891, 'Address: Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) 2021 Meshblock, Code'
variable_description: The mesh block the address Centrelink held for the person fell in, one row per address period on the location details table. The DSS registry defines mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" that "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", so it is the finest location DOMINO records for a person. MESHMATCH beside it says whether the code came from matching the address itself or only its coordinates, SA1_MAINCODE, SA2_MAINCODE, POSTCODE and STATE are the same address at coarser levels, and the column repeats on the temporary and terminated address table and on snap_domino_beta.
value_definition: An eleven-digit mesh block code. The PLIDA data item list labels this column ASGS 2016 while the DSS registry maps it to the ASGS 2021 mesh block data element, so confirm the edition against the extract's reference period before joining to boundary files.
limitation: A mesh block is not a dwelling or a household, so two people with the same code live in the same small area rather than the same home. The code also describes where Centrelink last recorded the person, so it lags an unreported move, and where MESHMATCH is blank the address never matched at all and the geography columns on the row are empty rather than wrong.
rationale: The LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps meshblock to the ASGS 2021 Meshblock data element, which publishes the ABS definition and the N(11) domain. The edition disagreement with the PLIDA data item list is why the confidence is medium rather than high.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Asgs 2016 meshblock' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not mention that the DSS registry now maps the same column to the 2021 standard.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54357, 'Address: Meshblock matched indicator, Code'
variable_description: Says how the mesh block on the same row was derived: from the address text, or from the coordinates behind it. The DSS registry defines it as an "Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates", which makes it the quality flag for every geography column on the location details table. It matters because a coordinate match can put a record on the wrong side of a boundary, so MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE are less reliable at fine resolution where this column reads L.
value_definition: One character: A where the mesh block was matched by address and L where it was matched by latitude and longitude. A blank is the registry's supplementary value, meaning the address was not matched at all.
limitation: It grades how the geocode was obtained, not whether the address was correct, so a stale or mistyped address that geocodes cleanly still returns A. It also says nothing about whether the person actually lived there, only about the matching step that produced the codes.
rationale: The registry maps loc_dtls.meshmatch to the Meshblock matched indicator data element, which publishes the definition, the A and L permissible values and the blank supplementary value.
evidence_quote: Indicator identifying if a meshblock code was matched by address or longitude/latitude coordinates.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so the two codes and their consequence for boundary accuracy went unstated.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry distribution 84485, 'STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA)'
variable_description: The month the person was born, held separately from YEAR_OF_BIRTH because the PLIDA release of DOMINO carries no full date of birth. The department's internal equivalent of this table, stt_pit_ext, holds a single date of birth as YYYY-MM-DD; the PLIDA version splits it into month and year, which is a disclosure control rather than a difference in what was collected. Combined with YEAR_OF_BIRTH it fixes a person's age to within a month, and AGE on the same row gives their age as at the extract date.
value_definition: A calendar month. The DSS registry restricts the metadata for this column, so neither the coding, the width nor the treatment of missing values is published, and the value should be inspected in the extract before use.
limitation: There is no day of birth, so an exact age on a given date cannot be calculated and anyone whose birthday falls in the month of an event sits on either side of an age threshold with equal probability. That matters for payments with sharp age tests, such as the move from Youth Allowance to JobSeeker Payment or reaching Age Pension age, where a month of uncertainty is enough to misclassify eligibility.
rationale: The registry's STATIC_DEMOGS (PLIDA) distribution lists month_of_birth and year_of_birth as columns but marks their data elements permission restricted, while the internal stt_pit_ext distribution for the same table lists a single date_of_birth field. That supports what the column is and why it exists, but publishes nothing about its value domain, so the status stays guessed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Birth month' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, and did not explain that the split from a full date of birth is the reason exact ages cannot be built.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108855, 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment'
variable_description: The income support payment the person moves onto next within the same active payment spell. With PREV_ISP it lets one snapshot row be read as a transition rather than a state: Parenting Payment Single to JobSeeker Payment as a youngest child ages out, or JobSeeker Payment to Disability Support Pension after a successful claim. Where the current payment is the last in the spell there is nothing to point to, and LAST_ACTIVE_ISP names the closing payment instead.
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, CAR for Carer Payment.
limitation: The next payment is scoped to the current spell, so a payment taken up after a break too long to be stitched into that spell never appears here. The column also carries no date, so it says a transition happened without saying when, and ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE bounds the whole spell rather than the changeover.
rationale: The registry binds snap_domino_beta.next_isp to 'Payment: Next Income Support Payment' and gives its value domain as the DSS benefit type code. That the field is empty at the end of a spell follows from the definition's scoping to the period of activity rather than being stated on the page.
evidence_quote: Refers to the next Income Support Payment type benefit (in this period of activity)
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without naming the benefit type code set or the spell scoping that decides when the field is empty.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 54775, 'Recipient: Object Type, Code'
variable_description: Says what kind of entity the demographic record describes: a person, a child, or an organisation. The DSS registry defines the column as containing "the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer", and it matters because DOMINO's customer records are not all adults with a claim of their own. Children listed on a carer's or a family payment record, and organisations acting as nominees or payees, sit in the same customer table, so this is the column that keeps them out of a count of recipients.
value_definition: A three-character code with three permissible values: PER, CHI and ORG. The registry publishes the codes without written meanings, so the expansions to person, child and organisation come from the code letters themselves.
limitation: It classifies the record, not a person's role in a payment: a CHI record does not say which payment the child was listed against or who claimed for them, and the relationship tables carry that link. Filtering to PER is also not the same as filtering to adults, because the object type follows how the record was created rather than the person's age now.
rationale: The registry maps static_demogs.object_type_code to 'Recipient: Object Type, Code' and publishes the three-value domain. The expansion of each code and the caution about age are read from the code letters and the table's contents rather than quoted.
evidence_quote: Contains the Object Type code (PER/CHI/ORG) for the Customer.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Object type code' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, when the domain has exactly three values and decides whether a row is a recipient at all.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108240, 'Partnered status'
variable_description: Says whether Centrelink had the person recorded as a member of a couple on the snapshot date. Partnered status drives rates, income tests and asset tests across almost every payment, so it explains rate differences on the snapshot table that ISP_TYPE_CODE alone cannot. EXT_DOM_HOUSEHOLD_ID pairs the person with their partner by concatenating the two DOMINO person identifiers, so a Y here should sit beside a two-person household identifier.
value_definition: One alphabetic character: Y for partnered and N for not partnered, with U as the registry's supplementary value for unknown. Three states can therefore appear.
limitation: It is a social security assessment of whether a couple relationship exists, not a marital status, so a de facto couple reads as Y and a married couple who have separated under one roof can read as N. It also refers only to the snapshot date and says nothing about how long the relationship had been recorded or how often it changed.
rationale: The registry maps snap_domino_beta.partnered_status to the 'Partnered status' data element and publishes the Y and N permissible values plus the U supplementary value.
evidence_quote: The active partnership status of a person, represented by a flag.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording and carried the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the unknown code and the difference between assessed couple status and marital status were both missing.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 615, 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The date a person's blindness was diagnosed, which is the qualifying date for the blind rate of Age Pension or Disability Support Pension. The DSS registry defines it as "The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". It is the only medical field on the static demographics table, and it belongs there rather than in the dated medical condition records because blind status is assessed once and then attaches to the person.
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. It is populated only for recipients assessed as permanently blind, so it is empty for almost every person on the table.
limitation: A populated date means blindness was diagnosed, not that the person was paid a blind pension from that date or paid at all; claim, grant and rate information sit in the payment history tables. It is also not an onset date, since it records the ophthalmologist's diagnosis rather than when sight was lost, and those can be years apart.
rationale: The registry maps static_demogs.pen_blind_start_date to 'Person: Blindness start date, YYYY-MM-DD' and publishes its definition and the YYYY-MM-DD date domain.
evidence_quote: The date upon which a recipient's blindness was diagnosed by an ophthalmologist, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Recipient pension blindness start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying who makes the assessment or that the date is a diagnosis rather than an onset.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 428, 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code'
variable_description: Says whether the concession card determination on this row was still pending rather than settled. The DSS registry defines it as an indicator of "whether a concession card is pending", so it is what separates a card the person actually held from a determination still in progress. It appears on all four concession card tables, covering the Health Care Card, the Pensioner Concession Card, the low income card and the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, and it should be read with CARD_ISSUE_DATE, CARD_START_DATE and CARD_END_DATE, because a pending row can carry a start date before any card was produced.
value_definition: One character, Y or N, with N as the registry's default. The field is boolean, so a row carrying no explicit value is treated as not pending.
limitation: It records the state of the determination when the row was written, not the eventual outcome, so a pending row is not evidence that the card was later granted or refused. Counting card holders without excluding pending rows overstates coverage, and the flag cannot tell you how long the determination stayed pending.
rationale: The CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps pending_flag to 'Payment: Concession card pending flag, Code', which publishes the definition, the Y and N values and the N default.
evidence_quote: Indicates whether a concession card is pending.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Concession card pending flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that including pending rows inflates a count of card holders.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 394, 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row stops applying, closing an episode that PERIOD_START_DATE opened. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Nearly every DOMINO table is built this way, with one row per person per period, whether the period covers an address, a concession card, a medical assessment, an income record or a payment component, so this column and its start-date partner are what make DOMINO longitudinal rather than a set of snapshots.
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain. Whether a still-open episode is left blank or carried with a sentinel far-future date varies between DOMINO tables, so check a column's maximum value before filtering on it.
limitation: The date closes an administrative record, not the circumstance behind it: an address period ends when the department was told of a change, not when the person moved, and a card period ends when the determination changed, not when the person stopped using the card. Periods on the same table can also abut or overlap after a retrospective correction, so counting rows is not the same as counting spells.
rationale: The registry maps period_end_date on the DOMINO distributions, including loc_dtls, ccd_hcc, mcd_dtls, inc_shc and the payment history tables, to the single data element 'Event: Period end date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event end date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, which said nothing about DOMINO's episode structure or about how open periods are represented.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 393, 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD'
variable_description: The day the record on this row starts applying. The DSS registry defines it as "The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD". Every DOMINO table that holds history is keyed on a person and this date, so to use any of them you filter the pair of period columns against a date of interest; without them a table is a stack of overlapping records with no time dimension. On tables such as loc_dtls and ccd_hcc one person has many rows, and the start dates are what put them in order.
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, ten characters, from the registry's Date YYYY-MM-DD value domain.
limitation: The start date is when the department recorded a circumstance as taking effect, not when it happened. A backdated grant carries an effective date earlier than the decision, and a late-reported address change carries one later than the move, so the column cannot be used to time real-world events precisely. It also marks the start of this record only, not of the person's dealings with the department.
rationale: The registry maps period_start_date across the DOMINO distributions to the single data element 'Event: Period start date, YYYY-MM-DD', which publishes its definition and its ten-character date domain.
evidence_quote: The date on which a reporting period relating to an event commences, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Event start date' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing on the gap between an administrative effective date and the event it stands for.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 174, 'Address: Australian postcode, Code'
variable_description: The postcode of the address Centrelink held for the person during this period. The DSS registry defines it as "The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address". On the location details table it is the coarse end of a set of geography columns that runs from MESHBLOCK up through SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE to STATE, and it is the one taken straight off the reported address rather than derived by geocoding, so it survives where MESHMATCH shows the address never matched. The same column repeats on snap_domino_beta and on the temporary and terminated address table.
value_definition: A four-digit code in the registry's Australian postcode code domain, which is Australia Post's set of postal delivery areas rather than an ABS statistical geography.
limitation: Postcodes are delivery areas, not statistical areas: a few cross state borders, some cover only post office boxes with no residents, and they do not nest inside SA2s or LGAs. Aggregating recipient counts by postcode and dividing by ABS regional populations therefore mismatches at the edges, and SA2_MAINCODE is the column to use instead.
rationale: The LOC_DTLS_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps postcode to 'Address: Australian postcode, Code', which publishes the definition and names the Australia Post derived value domain.
evidence_quote: The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area for an address.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Address postcode' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without warning that a postal geography does not align with ABS statistical areas.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 108854, 'Payment: Previous Income Support Payment'
variable_description: The income support payment the person was on immediately before the current one, within the same active payment spell. It is what lets a single snapshot row show a pathway rather than a state: a DSP row with JSP behind it is a successful disability claim, and a JSP row with PPS behind it is usually a single parent whose youngest child aged out of Parenting Payment Single. NEXT_ISP is the forward-looking partner, and FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP names where the spell began.
value_definition: A three or four character code from the DSS benefit type code set, which the registry defines as "A code set representing government benefits" and which covers about a hundred payments: AGE for Age Pension, JSP for JobSeeker Payment, DSP for Disability Support Pension, PPS for Parenting Payment Single.

The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income". The column exists because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income rather than taxable income, so the amounts a tax return leaves out are collected separately here alongside SHC_AN_SAL_SCF for salary sacrifice, SHC_AN_INC_FGN for foreign income and SHC_AN_PRP_LOS for net investment and property losses.
value_definition: An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN. It is zero for anyone with no employer, which is most card holders, since the card is aimed at people of Age Pension age.
limitation: It captures reportable fringe benefits for one income test, so it is not a measure of total remuneration and does not include compulsory employer superannuation contributions. A zero cannot be read as no employment either, only as no reportable benefits, so it is not a proxy for retirement.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_emp_ben to the Commonwealth Seniors Healthcare Card annual employer provided benefits data element, which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual employer-provided benefits a recipient receives, not included in taxable income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual employer provided benefits income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why an income test needs amounts left out of taxable income.

value_source: DSS Metadata Registry data element 501, 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency'
variable_description: Income from overseas sources counted for the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card income test, expressed in Australian dollars. The DSS registry defines it as "The amount of annual foreign income a recipient receives". It is collected because the card is tested on adjusted taxable income, so a retiree living on an overseas pension is tested on that income even where it does not appear on an Australian tax return, and SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same row holds the domestic taxable amount.
value_definition: An annual amount in Australian dollars to two decimal places, format N[9].NN, converted from the source currency. Unlike the deemed income on the same row it is a reported figure rather than a calculated one.
limitation: It does not say where the income came from or what kind it was, so an overseas age pension, foreign rent and offshore investment income collapse into one number and no country can be identified. Because it is reported only for a card income test, it appears only for people who claimed or held the card and cannot be used to measure foreign income among older Australians generally.
rationale: The INC_SHC_EXT (PLIDA) distribution maps shc_an_inc_fgn to 'Recipient: Annual foreign income, Total Australian currency', which publishes the definition and the N[9].NN currency domain.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual foreign income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual foreign income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with no currency, no units and no note that the figure exists only for card claimants.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The taxable income Centrelink held for a person when testing them for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). The inc_shc table carries one row per annual reporting period, bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, for people whose card eligibility was assessed. This column is one of seven income components on the row: deemed income, foreign income, employer provided benefits, net property and investment losses and salary sacrificed income sit beside it and are added to it to reach the adjusted taxable income the card is tested against. It answers what the card decision was based on, not what the person earned in total.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, unlike DOMINO's other income tables which hold a daily rate. The figure is what was reported to or held by Centrelink for the card assessment, and the external release applies variable rounding to the amount so that a person cannot be recognised from an unusual value.
limitation: It is not the person's ATO assessment. Centrelink records the taxable income relevant to the card test at the time of the test, so it can predate, lag or differ from the assessed figure in the ATO products in PLIDA, and it is only present for people whose seniors card eligibility was assessed rather than for all older Australians. Reading it as household income is also wrong: a couple is tested on combined income, but this row belongs to one person.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_shc_ext as the longitudinal history of annually reported Centrelink income tied to seniors health card eligibility, and gives each column of the table its own definition, including this one.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried only the custodian's label 'Seniors healthcare card income - annual taxable income' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence as both its value definition and its limitation, so nothing said what the figure was for or how it related to the six income columns beside it.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: An estimate of a year's taxable income used for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card assessment where an assessed figure was not available, defined by DSS as "The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). It sits directly beside SHC_AN_INC_TXB on the same annual row, which is the assessed rather than the estimated amount. Estimates arise when someone claims the card before a tax assessment exists for the relevant year, typically at retirement or on a first claim. The pair together shows whether the card decision rested on an estimate or on a settled figure.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: A dollar amount for a whole year, on the same footing as the assessed taxable income column and subject to the same variable rounding in the external release. It records what was estimated at the time of the assessment, not a revised figure.
limitation: The column cannot tell you which figure decided entitlement, nor whether the estimate was later replaced once a tax assessment issued. An estimate present alongside an assessed amount is not evidence of a dispute or of ineligibility, and the difference between the two is not an error measure: they can refer to different income years.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines every column of inc_shc_ext, including the estimated taxable income field, and describes the table as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual estimated taxable income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the custodian's label and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so a reader could not tell an estimate from the assessed amount held in the next column.

value_domain: Annual loss amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: The investment and rental property losses added back when a person's income is tested for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, which DSS defines as "The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Losses are added back because they reduce taxable income without reducing a person's capacity to support themselves, so the adjusted taxable income used for the card is higher than the taxable income beside it. A non-zero value here therefore raises the tested income rather than lowering it.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: An annual dollar amount standing for a loss rather than a receipt, reported for the same year as the other income columns on the row and variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: The column does not separate a negatively geared rental property from a geared share portfolio, so it cannot be used to identify property investors. It also says nothing about the asset behind the loss, which is tested separately under the assets test and is not carried in this table, and the sign convention is not published, so check the direction of the values before adding them to taxable income.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives this column its own definition inside the inc_shc_ext distribution, which it documents as the annual income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual property and net investment losses a recipient incurs.
supersedes_rationale: The entry restated the label 'annual net investment/property loss' and used one generic sentence for both the value definition and the limitation, so it never explained that a loss increases the income the card is tested on.

value_domain: Annual income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
variable_description: Income a person gave up under a salary sacrifice arrangement, counted back into the income test for a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card and defined by DSS as "The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_shc_ext). Like the property and investment loss column beside it, it is added back because sacrificing salary lowers taxable income without lowering the resources available to the person. For a card cohort at or near Age Pension age it usually reflects reportable contributions to superannuation made in the last working years.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_shc_ext
value_definition: An annual dollar amount reported for the same year as the other income components on the row, variably rounded in the external release.
limitation: It is a measure of reportable sacrificed income, not of superannuation saving: compulsory employer contributions are outside it, so the column understates what went into a fund and cannot be used to study contribution behaviour. Nor does it say what the salary was sacrificed for, since sacrificed income can go to a car, an expense package or a fund.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside inc_shc_ext, the distribution it documents as the annual Centrelink income history behind seniors health card eligibility.
evidence_quote: The amount of annual salary sacrificed income a recipient receives.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's label, which even carries a typo ('sacrified'), and gave the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: The day the Snap-DOMINO row describes, defined by DSS as "A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). Everything else on the row is measured as at that day: the on-snap flags for income support, family payments, rent assistance and supplementary payments, the concession cards held, the address and its geography, age, partnered status and principal carer status. Snap-DOMINO exists so that a cross-section can be taken without assembling episodes from the underlying event tables, so this column, with the person key, is what makes a row unique.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, taking one of the fixed reference days on which the snapshot is cut rather than any day a person had a dealing with the agency.
limitation: It marks a chosen observation day, so anything that started and ended between two snapshot days is invisible: a short spell on a payment, a card that lapsed and was reissued, or a move and a move back. Rates built from Snap-DOMINO are point-in-time prevalence, not incidence, and comparing two snap dates measures stocks rather than flows.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT as snapshot views of individuals' interactions with the welfare system on specified days of the year, and defines this column as the reference date those derived items hang off.
evidence_quote: A primary reference date for derived items in Snap-Domino, recorded as a day of a month of a year, and represented as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's wording and then said only that no finite value list applies, twice, so nothing explained that every other column on the row is measured as at this date.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
variable_description: The day an address became the recipient's effective address in Centrelink's records, opening the location episode the rest of the row describes. The loc_derived table holds one row per episode: the hashed address register identifier, the address type and priority, and the mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state codings of that address under ASGS 2021. Read with END_DATE it gives a residential history assembled from welfare administration rather than from a survey, and ADDR_PRTY exists because a person can hold more than one open address at once.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, as every date column in DOMINO's location distributions is.
limitation: It dates a record, not a removal van. The address becomes effective when the person tells the agency or the agency updates its records, so a start date can trail a move by weeks or months and a person who stops dealing with Centrelink keeps an address that is no longer theirs. Episodes across address types can also overlap, so a start date here does not close the previous episode.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution as derived location boundaries and lists its contents: the anonymised address register identifier, the address priority code, the address type and the ASGS 2021 geography, with dates carried in YYYY-MM-DD form. The registry does not publish this column under the PLIDA name START_DATE, so the shape is sourced and the reading of the date as the start of the address episode is written from the table's contents.
evidence_quote: Derived code highlighting address priority for identifying the location of a recipient on a given day.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Effective address start date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say what the episode was, what closed it, or why more than one address can be open at once.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
variable_description: The state or territory of the address held for the person, defined by DSS as "The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, loc_dtls_ext). Which address that is depends on the table: loc_dtls holds home addresses, loc_pos_temp_term_dtls holds postal, temporary and term addresses, and snap_domino_beta holds the address as at the snapshot day. On the location tables the column sits with POSTCODE, MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE for the same address, so it is the coarsest of several geographies for one place rather than a separate fact.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution loc_dtls_ext
value_definition: A short character code rather than a name: the registry gives the column as a character string of up to three characters, so the values are the usual state and territory abbreviations rather than numbers. Snap-DOMINO's STATE_CODE, by contrast, is a one-digit numeric code, so the two columns cannot be compared without recoding.
limitation: The state belongs to an address on file, not to a person, so a stale record puts someone in the state they left. On the postal and temporary address table the value can be a mailing state or a term address for a student, which is not where the person lives, and MESHMATCH warns that the finer geography beside it may have been matched from coordinates rather than from the address itself.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines loc_dtls_ext as the location of an individual's home addresses in DOMINO and gives this column its own definition; the companion distribution loc_pos_temp_term_dtls_ext, documented as non-home addresses, carries the same column.
evidence_quote: The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Address state' and used one generic sentence for both the definition and the limitation, so it did not distinguish the home address table from the postal, temporary and term address table where the same column means something different.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
variable_description: The state or territory of a location episode as coded to the ABS geography, defined by DSS as "The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, LOC_DERIVED). It is the top of a coding chain on the same row: the mesh block, SA1, SA2 and SA4 columns beside it code the same address to finer ASGS 2021 areas, all derived from the address rather than reported by the person. Unlike STATE in loc_dtls, which travels with the recorded address, this is what the geocoding produced for the address that the episode's ARID stands for.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA)
value_definition: A single-digit ASGS state and territory code: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 the Northern Territory, 8 the Australian Capital Territory and 9 Other Territories.
limitation: It is the state of an address episode, not of a person on a given day, and a person with overlapping episodes can appear in two states at once, which is what ADDR_PRTY is there to resolve. It also says nothing about where a payment was administered or assessed, so it should not be used as a service-delivery region, and an address that could not be geocoded contributes no code at all rather than an unknown-state code.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents the loc_derived distribution and defines this column as the state or territory of an address represented by a code; the ASGS single-digit state and territory codes are the ABS standard the 2021 suffix names.
evidence_quote: The state or territory of an address, as represented by a code.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said only 'State (number)' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say which classification the number came from or how it related to the mesh block and SA codes beside it.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: The state or territory a person was located in on the snapshot day, which DSS documents with the note that "Australian states and territories are identified by unique one-digit codes" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). It is one of a stack of geography columns on the Snap-DOMINO row: postcode, mesh block, SA2, SA3, SA4, local government area, greater capital city area and Commonwealth electoral division all describe the same address as at SNAP_DATE. Snap-DOMINO also carries STATE and REPORTED_STATE, so the row holds more than one view of the same thing.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A one-digit code for the state or territory, in the ABS ordering that runs from New South Wales through the Australian Capital Territory and then the other territories.
limitation: The registry does not say which of the snapshot's state columns takes precedence, so treat a disagreement between this and REPORTED_STATE as a sign of address quality rather than assuming one is wrong. The code also fixes a person to one day: someone who moved interstate a week after the snapshot is counted in the state they left.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the Snap-DOMINO distribution and reproduces the definition of this column, which states the one-digit form of the code; the surrounding geography columns are listed on the same page.
evidence_quote: Australian states and territories are identified by unique one-digit codes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's sentence about one-digit codes and then the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it never said that the code describes the snapshot day, or that two other state columns sit on the same row.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
variable_description: The day a course event stops for the student it belongs to, defined by DSS as "End date for a student of a course event" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, edu_ftb_ext). Whose study it is depends on the table: in edu_ftb the course belongs to a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child, whose study is what keeps an older teenager an FTB child, while in edu_dtls it is the recipient's own course, which is what supports a student payment. COURSE_LVL, COURSE_TYPE and INST_TYPE describe the course, and STDNT_PRTCPN_STS says whether the student was still participating.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, recorded against a course event rather than an academic year.
limitation: An end date is not a completion. CMPLTN_IND and CMPLTN_DATE carry whether the course was finished, so a course event can close because the student left, changed institution or stopped being assessed for the payment. The date can also be the end expected when the course was recorded rather than the day study actually stopped.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside edu_ftb_ext, documented as the longitudinal history of FTB related educational information, and the same column with the same definition sits in edu_dtls_ext, documented as historical details of educational courses undertaken by a recipient.
evidence_quote: End date for a student of a course event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Student end date for course' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not distinguish a course ending from a course being completed, nor the child's study in edu_ftb from the recipient's own study in edu_dtls.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
variable_description: The day a course event starts for the student it belongs to, defined by DSS as "Start date for a student of a course event" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, edu_ftb_ext). In edu_ftb the student is a Family Tax Benefit recipient's child and the course is the study that keeps that child qualifying; in edu_dtls the student is the recipient, and the course supports a student payment such as Youth Allowance, Austudy or ABSTUDY. With STDNT_END_DATE it bounds a spell of recorded study, which is the closest DOMINO comes to an education history for a welfare population.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution edu_ftb_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, recorded against a course event rather than an enrolment record held by the institution.
limitation: It dates the course as Centrelink recorded it for a payment purpose, not enrolment at the provider, so study that never touched a payment leaves no row at all. A student who changes course or provider starts a new event, so consecutive rows are not evidence of a break in study, and two overlapping rows are not evidence of two concurrent courses.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column inside edu_ftb_ext, documented as the longitudinal history of FTB related educational information, and carries the same column in edu_dtls_ext for courses undertaken by the recipient.
evidence_quote: Start date for a student of a course event.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Student start date for course' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so it did not say whose study is recorded or that a course event is a Centrelink record rather than an enrolment.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: Whether a supplementary payment was current for the person on the snapshot day, defined by DSS as a "Flag indicating supplementary benefit received on snap date" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). Supplementary payments in DOMINO are the additions to a person's circumstances rather than a main income support payment: the type code list covers Carer Allowance, Double Orphan Pension, Parental Leave Pay, Dad and Partner Pay, Assistance for Isolated Children, the ABSTUDY Pensioner Education Supplement and Youth Training Allowance. The flag is one of a matched set with ISP_ON_SNAP, FTBA_ON_SNAP, FTBB_ON_SNAP and RENT_ON_SNAP, so a person's whole payment position on the day can be read across five columns.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A boolean flag on the snapshot row, set from whether a supplementary payment was active on SNAP_DATE.
limitation: It does not say which supplementary payment, or how many: a person receiving Carer Allowance and Parental Leave Pay looks the same as a person receiving one of them. SUP_TYPE_CODE names the type and SUP_BEN_STATUS gives its status, so the flag alone cannot support any statement about a particular programme.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes this column's definition on the Snap-DOMINO distribution, and its companion value domain, Payment: Supplementary Type Code, lists the payments the supplementary group covers.
evidence_quote: Flag indicating supplementary benefit received on snap date
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's sentence, left the value domain as 'not specified' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence for both definition and limitation, so nothing said what counts as a supplementary payment.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
variable_description: How long the person was active on a supplementary payment, given by DSS as the "Number of days active on supplementary benefit" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT). It is the duration counterpart to SUP_ON_SNAP: the flag says whether a supplementary payment was current on the snapshot day, and this column says how many days of activity lie behind it. The same pairing exists for income support, both parts of Family Tax Benefit and rent assistance, so intensity and point-in-time receipt can be compared across payment groups on one row.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT
value_definition: A whole number of days, held as a count of up to eight digits on the underlying data element, Payment: Supplementary Panel Days.
limitation: The registry does not publish the window the days are counted over, so the count cannot be turned into a share of a period without an assumption about the panel. Days active is also not days paid: a payment can be current while the rate is nil, and the count says nothing about which supplementary payment ran or whether the days were continuous.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry defines this column on the Snap-DOMINO distribution and, on the underlying data element Payment: Supplementary Panel Days, gives its form as an eight-digit count while documenting no window over which the days are counted.
evidence_quote: Number of days active on supplementary benefit
supersedes_rationale: The entry copied the custodian's sentence and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say that the counting window is undocumented, which is the first thing anyone using the number needs.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person key every DOMINO table is joined on, described by DSS as "A synthetic numeric sequence of characters used for the purposes of identifying a unique DOMINO entity" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, CCD_HCC_EXT). One value ties a person's payment history, income, concession cards, addresses, relationships, education and medical assessments together across the sixty-odd tables that carry it, which is what makes DOMINO a longitudinal record rather than a set of extracts. Within PLIDA the same key runs across products: MBS, PBS, the tax products, Census and the rest carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID under the same custodian description, Synthetic MADIP Person ID, so a DOMINO row joins to another agency's row on this column directly rather than through a separate mapping file.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution CCD_HCC_EXT (PLIDA)
value_definition: A numeric identifier assigned for linkage, with no meaning in its digits. It is not a Centrelink customer reference number and carries nothing about the person, so it can be matched but not decoded.
limitation: It identifies one person, not a household or an income unit, so it cannot be used to assemble a family: EXT_DOM_PARTNER_ID, CHILD_ID and the other listed-person identifiers on the same rows are a separate numbering space and do not equal another person's value here. A person absent from DOMINO is a person with no dealings with the department rather than a person with no need, and a person who fails to join to another PLIDA product has no record there rather than no history: the key is only as complete as the linkage behind it.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry gives the column its definition on every DOMINO distribution released to PLIDA, including the health care card determination table this occurrence sits in, and the PLIDA data item list names it as the synthetic MADIP person identifier held against the agency spine.
evidence_quote: A synthetic numeric sequence of characters used for the purposes of identifying a unique DOMINO entity.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID' with a value domain of 'Opaque identifier (inferred)' and the generic no-value-list sentence in both fields, so across 64 occurrences it never said what the key joins, or that a cross-agency join has to go through the spine.

value_domain: Daily income amount in Australian dollars
value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_tac_ext
variable_description: Income attributed to a person from a private trust or private company they are connected to, defined by DSS as the "Amount of income derived by a recipient from a trust or company" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, inc_tac_ext). The column exists because social security law looks through private structures: where a person controls or benefits from a trust or company, its income is attributed to them and tested like their own. The inc_tac table holds nothing else about the entity, so the row is the person, the period bounded by PERIOD_START_DATE and PERIOD_END_DATE, and this amount.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution inc_tac_ext
value_definition: A daily dollar rate rather than a period total, held to two decimal places in a format of up to nine digits before the point. A period figure is the rate multiplied by the days in the period, and the external release variably rounds the amount.
limitation: The attributed amount follows social security rules, not tax rules, so it will not reconcile with a trust distribution in the same person's income tax return in the ATO products. It also names neither the trust nor the company and gives no share of control, so two people attributed income from the same entity cannot be identified as connected.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents inc_tac_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink reported income from trusts and companies in DOMINO, and gives this column its own definition and its decimal format.
evidence_quote: Amount of income derived by a recipient from a trust or company.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Trust and company daily income amount' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so it did not say why a welfare dataset holds trust income or that the figure is an attribution under means-test rules.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity closes on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as "The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). The mcd_dtls table is the record of medical conditions and work capacity assessments behind disability and participation decisions, holding the primary and secondary condition codes, an impairment rating, and the assessed hours a person can work. This date and its start-date pair bound the window in which the assessment treats the limitation as temporary rather than continuing.
description_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
value_definition: A date in YYYY-MM-DD form, set by an assessment rather than by a payment event.
limitation: The close of a temporary limitation is not recovery and not a payment change: the condition codes and the impairment rating on the same row can be unchanged, and whether anything happened to the person's payment is in the payment history tables, not here. A date in the future is the period the assessment set, not an observed end.
rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry documents mcd_dtls_ext as the longitudinal history of Centrelink medical conditions and work capacity assessments in DOMINO, and defines each of the capacity date columns individually.
evidence_quote: The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment ends, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD.
supersedes_rationale: The entry said 'Temporary limited capacity end date' and gave the generic no-value-list sentence as both definition and limitation, so it did not say the date comes from an assessment or how it relates to the assessed hours on the same row.

value_source: DSS Aristotle metadata registry, distribution mcd_dtls_ext
variable_description: The day a period of temporarily limited work capacity opens on a medical assessment, defined by DSS as "The date on which a period of temporary limited capacity relating to a recipient's medical condition assessment starts, expressed as YYYY-MM-DD" (DSS Aristotle metadata registry, mcd_dtls_ext). It marks when an assessor accepted that a condition limits what the person can do for a bounded time, which is the distinction that separates a temporary exemption from participation requirements from a continuing incapacity.
